title: Heuristic Retry Coach & Payload Composer — compact assistant for failed-request triage
creator: Leo Martinez
description:
Problem: engineers spend time hunting whether a failed request should be retried, how to retry it, and what the cost/quality trade-off is for different retry strategies. Current failed-request cards in the Console surface the error and raw payload, but teams repeatedly ask for prescriptive next steps and safe defaults when triaging production issues.

Goal: design a compact, optional 'Retry Coach' micro-panel attached to failed-request rows and the detailed payload view. The coach will: 1) classify the error (transient, throttling, model-quality, input validation), 2) recommend a retry mode (no-retry, idempotent, exponential-backoff, ballot/ensemble) with rationale, 3) show an estimated success probability and token-cost delta, and 4) provide a one-click 'Compose safe retry' that pre-populates payload changes (e.g., temperature, max_tokens, prompt chunking, KV cache bypass) in an editable composer.

Scope: prototype interactions for both the compact failed-request list (summary card) and the full Request Inspector modal. Include a lightweight computation model for cost delta and outcome probability (heuristic-based, not ML in v1). Provide accessibility patterns, keyboard-first flow for rapid triage, and an opt-out setting at org level.

Deliverables: Figma prototype (compact card + modal composer), interaction spec for engineering (APIs and telemetry points), copy deck for coach rationales, and a short experiment plan for A/B rollout measuring "time-to-resolution" and "unsafe retry rate".

Non-goals: Not shipping a machine-learning prediction service in v1; no automated retries executed without explicit user confirmation.
design_notes: Use a two-tier UI: compact coach at list level (icon + 1-line rationale) and expanded composer in Request Inspector.
Prioritize visibility of cost delta (tokens * price/unit) to discourage blind high-cost retries.
Default suggested retry mode should follow safety-first ordering: no-retry -> idempotent -> exponential-backoff -> ballot.
Keep composer changes declarative; do not change user prompts until user clicks 'Apply and Retry'.
Provide an affordance to pin coach suggestions to a route/model so platform engineers can create org-wide rules later.
comments: 2025-02-14 Leo Martinez: Kickoff completed with PM (Nina Rao) and Eng leads. Agreed heuristics for error taxonomy: network, rate-limit, model-hang, content-rejection, input-parse.
2025-02-17 Maya Patel: Initial sketches uploaded to Figma, included a compact chip with color-coded taxonomy badges. Shared with Design Guild for early feedback.
2025-02-19 Eng feedback (Santiago Ruiz): ask to expose telemetry points: suggestion_id, heuristic_version, estimated_probability, cost_delta_tokens. Also flagged backend gating for composer defaults.
2025-02-21 PM review (Nina Rao): requested explicit 'why we recommend this' microcopy for auditability and a link to the rollout policy that will be used by Dedicated customers.
2025-02-23 Design critique: prefer neutral color palette for 'no-retry' vs warning palette for 'high-risk' retries. Accessibility check: ensure 4.5:1 contrast on rationale badges.
2025-02-25 Prototype updated: composer now supports 'suggested edits' diff view; added telemetry hooks. Ready for Eng intake and feasibility spike (ENG-84098).
notes_for_engineering: Provide an API endpoint to retrieve coach suggestions for a request id: /v1/requests/{id}/retry-suggestions
Telemetry events: suggestion_shown, suggestion_accepted, suggestion_rejected, retry_executed; include fields: heuristic_version, suggestion_id, estimated_probability, cost_delta_tokens.
Composer should return a minimal patch (json-patch style) describing suggested field edits to the original payload.
Fallback behavior: if heuristics cannot classify, present 'manual triage' path with copy tips and links to debugging docs.
